why_trail.why: This gate is a cutover of the READ path only: the same filename appears on both sides of the cut, so the operative distinction is per-mention, not per-file. 5 of 11 skills/ files carrying the name hold intake; COMMANDER_SPINE holds 5 mentions of which exactly 2 are intake and 3 are the writer. The acceptance guard is phrasing-independent (6 regex markers over a git-grep enumeration) precisely because a hand-written site list is the defect class this issue consolidates -- so the guard, not my reading, decides completeness.

Sites 1 and 3 are compound sentences carrying two things; only the lessons conjunct is cut, so both files keep a standalone invariants clause rather than losing the bullet. Site 2 sits in the LATITUDE task, not the context task -- the earlier enumeration that missed it looked for the context step by name. ADMIRAL_SPINE went 3 LESSONS.md lines to 2, keeping the closeout writer at :49 and the verify_lessons_applied check at :57.

The Charter guide bullet is the one site where the file's REMAINING mention is itself the write path, so the line survives and only its clause structure changes: the read instruction is replaced with the positive statement of what the bank now is (a staging bank an audit drains, not planning input for a live run), which is the doctrine a Charter-compiled guide should carry after the cutover. Wording deliberately avoids the token 'read' anywhere before the filename so it cannot re-trip the guard's broadest marker.

Probed the writer trio against the guard's six regexes BEFORE editing: lines 109/112/125 match ZERO markers, so cutting only sites 5 and 6 greens the guard with no pressure to touch the writer -- the over-reach risk was measurable in advance, not just warned about. Measured blast radius corrects the handoff: only ONE of the three named test_episode_capture tests actually read the shipped declaration (the other two already build synthetic entries and passed untouched), so the real failure set was 1 test in each of the two files. Reworked that one onto a synthetic path while ADDING an assertion that no durable declaration ships, which converts a test that would have silently changed subject into one that fails if a durable entry returns.

Read the guard's OUTPUT, not its exit code: enumeration moved 11 -> 10 files because LAUNCH_ORDER lost its only mention and left the git-grep set entirely, and AGENT_GUIDE still emits an advisory NOTE because it correctly keeps one write-path mention. Neither is a site hiding from the guard. Suite total is unchanged at 1621 (was 2 failed + 1619 passed), which is the mechanical proof the reworked tests were reworked and not deleted. 8 source files changed; the other 3 paths in git diff --stat are the Commander's pre-existing engine state, attributed by grepping my session id out of them rather than assumed.
